message.content: In domestic cats and many wild felids, the presence of a mane in males is governed by a dominant allele at the **androgen‑receptor (AR)** locus. In lions, the “mane” phenotype is expressed when at least one copy of this dominant allele is present, whereas females (who typically lack a mane) carry two copies of the recessive allele. Thus, the dominant genetic trait responsible for the iconic mane in male lions is the dominant allele at the AR gene.
